title: No Internet? No Problem! RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das Boosts Offline Digital Payments
description: RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das recently announced expanded rules for offline digital payments. This means you can now make small payments up to ₹500 even withou.

faq.q: What devices support offline digital payments?
faq.a: Currently, these payments are typically supported by smartphones through specific payment apps or digital wallets that have integrated the RBI's offline payment framework. Feature phones may also be enabled for simpler versions.

faq.q: How do I enable this feature on my phone?
faq.a: The exact steps will depend on your payment app or bank. Usually, you'll find an option within your app to activate "offline payments" or "tap and pay" and link it to your bank account or load a pre-paid balance.

faq.q: What happens if my phone is lost or stolen?
faq.a: Since there are limits on individual transactions (₹500) and the total amount (₹2,000) that can be held offline, the risk is contained. You should report the loss to your bank or payment service provider immediately, just like you would with a lost debit card.

faq.q: Is there a fee for making offline payments?
faq.a: The RBI aims to keep digital payments affordable. While specific charges might vary by service provider, the general push is for low or no transaction fees for small-value digital payments.

faq.q: Can I use offline payments for large purchases?
faq.a: No, the current framework is designed for small-value transactions, with a limit of ₹500 per transaction and a total limit of ₹2,000 on the device. For larger purchases, you will still need to use online payment methods.

fact_check.summary: The article is largely accurate regarding the details of offline digital payments, including transaction limits and the overall aim of financial inclusion. However, it incorrectly states the date of the announcement and the name of the RBI Governor at that time.
